ALL 107 CHAPTERS ARE AUTHORED. 1,133 entities, 4,529 exact mentions in original-en and 4,672 in modern-en, nothing omitted from either edition, 285 focused tests passing, content revision 2026-09-13.13. Every chapter of both full English editions has been read paragraph by paragraph over fourteen passes, and the scope line now says 'all 107 chapters' rather than a range. The six Editorial checks of AUTOMATION-QUEUE.md have been run over the whole work and the answers are written into the package README: (1) namesakes -- 282 entities in the README table, 215 rows, each pinned by a test; (2) person or not -- every deliberate exclusion listed, with the reason; (3) scriptural and mythological references -- checked, and the figures left unbound named; (4) ambiguous and generic references -- bound only where the text settles them, the rest listed; (5) spot-read -- run over every range as it was authored, and a FRESH WHOLE-WORK SPOT-READ of forty mentions drawn at random from all 107 chapters and both editions after the last chapter, every one of the forty correct; (6) both editions independently -- the edition-asymmetry census run over all 107 chapters, omittedEntities empty in both editions, and the forty-one remaining asymmetries each read and classed into three kinds, none of them a wrong card.

NEXT, AND THIS LANE DOES NOT DO IT: release review and app integration. This lane never sets appStatus, which stays not-integrated. Two decisions belong to the release owner and are written up under 'What is left, and what was learned' in the README. FIRST, the eighteen citation abbreviations: the older edition writes Hor., Claud., Quintil., Lucret., Propert., Liv., Cic., Mart. and Aug. where the modern edition expands the author's name, so those mentions bind in the modern edition alone. Closing them means adding each abbreviation as an alias on nine authors; it was not done because an abbreviation is not a name, and the release owner may decide the other way. SECOND, Fortune: she is deliberately not cast, with the Christian God, Christ, Satan and Nature, although chapter 33 personifies her throughout and chapter 69 again. That is the one scope decision in the package a reader might disagree with.

THIRTEEN SOURCE DEFECTS are recorded for the release owner and were not repaired; no edition byte was touched. They are listed in full in the README under 'Source defects -- recorded, not repaired', and they fall into four kinds: a LACUNA at 90:7 where the older edition's sentence is broken and names nobody; MISPRINTS carried as aliases exactly as printed (Lactantms, Zenocrates, Metellius, Origeti, Titius Livius, EPICUYUS TO HEYMACHUS, Diogeries, Thamus, Euxodus, Critolaiis, Perrete, Aulus Gelliusor, and the corrupt Latin of 100:46 and 100:43 which both editions share); STRUCTURAL defects, where a note has landed in the wrong place (102:1 belongs to 101:13, one chapter earlier) or a sentence runs across a note (69:468/469, 101:7/101:9); and one MISTRANSLATION, at 74:120, where the older edition renders Acts i. 26 as 'The lot fell upon Matthew' and the text has Matthias. Two further divergences are NOT defects and must not be 'fixed': the modern edition drops 'says Seneca' from 70:35 and writes 'Plato's ring' at 73:64 where the older has the adjective 'the Platonic ring'.

THE EIGHT LESSONS THIS BOOK TAUGHT, in the order of how much each one caught, are written up in the README for whoever authors the next book. The first is the one to carry: LIST EVERY OCCURRENCE OF A NAME ACROSS THE WHOLE WORK BEFORE CHOOSING BETWEEN AN ALIAS AND A KEY. It found fourteen entities cast nowhere at all in chapters that had already been signed off -- Xenocrates, the Muses, the Sirens, Origen, Strato, Messalina, Philoxenus, Scipio Africanus, Metrocles, Voltaire, Circe, Archimedes, Ceres and Eudoxus, five of those six passes reaching back into chapter 69 -- and it stopped four mis-bindings before the first build. Chapter 69, the Apology, is the chapter this package corrected most often after declaring it done. Do not read a clean audit as a finished chapter.
